text:
Mark Scheifele spent a week in November rewriting the Jets' record book. On Nov. 14 in Chicago he had four points and a shootout goal as Winnipeg came back from four goals down, and the Winnipeg Free Press' Ken Wiebe wrote that he "now stands alone as the franchise points leader." A week later against Vegas, his tying goal passed Dale Hawerchuk for the most goals in Jets history, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted. NHL.com's headline put it best: Scheifele surpasses Hawerchuk (again).

The production is real, and so is some luck, in different places. He has 31 points in 25 games and 19 in his last ten, but the team has scored 5.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which pads the assists. His own shooting runs the other way: 8 goals on 10.1 expected. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 11.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey's counterweight: opponents got more chances with him on the ice than with all but 3% of forwards. Our numbers project about 104 points.
headline: Mark Scheifele rewrites the Jets record book
